# tosijs-3d

> Declarative 3D/XR framework built on Babylon.js and the tosijs web component framework.

Version 0.13.0.

- Docs: https://3d.tosijs.net
- Source: https://github.com/tonioloewald/tosijs-3d
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/tosijs-3d

Each link below is the page's markdown. Drop `index.md` from it for the HTML page, where the examples run.
The whole corpus, as one markdown file: https://3d.tosijs.net/llms-full.txt

Live examples run inline on the shared page by default (not sandboxed):
each has its own `preview` element, but they share one tosijs module, so
`tosi()` state singletons are shared across every example on a page. This is
deliberate (it shows tosi isolation and lets you drive demos via the global
singleton). Namespace example state with unique top-level keys so examples
don't clobber each other; the `iframe` attribute isolates DOM/CSS, not state.

## Docs

- [tosijs-3d](https://3d.tosijs.net/index.md): Tosijs-3d is a library for building 3D web apps — and standalone apps, if that is what you want. Under the hood it uses Babylon.js for rendering, glTF/GLB
- [Getting started](https://3d.tosijs.net/getting-started/index.md): From nothing to a lit scene you can walk around, then where to go next.

## Demos

- [Demos](https://3d.tosijs.net/demos/index.md): Whole scenes you can walk around in, rather than one component at a time.

- [Solar System](https://3d.tosijs.net/solar-system/index.md): Our own solar system, built from the parts the rest of this site documents: every planet and moon a planet, the giants banded and ringed (gas-giant), the…
- [Weapon Fit](https://3d.tosijs.net/weapon-fit/index.md): Dial a weapon into a character's hand and copy out the numbers. A biped, a weapon library, and a panel of coordinates wired to the thing you are looking
- [hold grips](https://3d.tosijs.net/hold-grip/index.md): One grip per kind of thing held, not per item. A pistol and an SMG are held the same way, and so are a dagger and a long sword, so where the hand holds an…
- [hand socket](https://3d.tosijs.net/hand-socket/index.md): Where a hand holds things, on any rig. A hand bone's axes are the rig maker's choice, so a grip dialled in against one rig's bone holds the item at a…
- [Rig tool](https://3d.tosijs.net/rig-tool/index.md): Put a character on our animations, give it hair or a tail, and save the result. Pick one of the demo characters or load your own GLB.
- [Effect tool](https://3d.tosijs.net/effect-tool/index.md): Make an effect: particles, light and sound on one clock. Start from a preset (a volcano at any activity, a geyser, a splash, an explosion, a fireball…
- [Character Builder](https://3d.tosijs.net/character-builder/index.md): Make a person, and watch them walk. The first steps of the character creator (CHARACTER-DESIGN.md): MakeHuman's CC0 body (human-pack), reshaped by sliders…
- [human-pack](https://3d.tosijs.net/human-pack/index.md): A human pack is a base body as data: its mesh, its joints and its shape targets, converted from MakeHuman's CC0 assets by static-assets'…
- [character-file](https://3d.tosijs.net/character-file/index.md): A character as one JSON document: everything the character builder sets (where the body comes from, its shape, skin, eyes, face, hair, clothes and their…
- [character-store](https://3d.tosijs.net/character-store/index.md): The characters this browser keeps: the character builder saves here (the figure you are working on, and named ones), and any page on
- [human-morph](https://3d.tosijs.net/human-morph/index.md): The body sliders of the character creator (CHARACTER-DESIGN.md), as pure functions over a human pack: which targets a body uses and how much, and the sum…
- [human-rig](https://3d.tosijs.net/human-rig/index.md): UAL's 65-joint skeleton on a human pack's body, placed from the body itself: every joint is the centre of one of MakeHuman's joint cubes, small groups of…
- [tailor tool](https://3d.tosijs.net/tailor-tool/index.md): Cut a garment out of a body, and hand it back. Draw an outline over the body's front view and the skin inside it, front and back, becomes cloth: a…
- [tailor-recipe](https://3d.tosijs.net/tailor-recipe/index.md): A tailor's garment as a RECIPE that fits any body: its outlines, its thickness and how it is made (cut from the skin, a skirt, draped cloth), plus where…
- [tailor panel](https://3d.tosijs.net/tailor-panel/index.md): The tailor, always on the system bar, and the wardrobe it keeps. This is the character builder's tailor as a piece any page with a character can mount: a…
- [skin-tone](https://3d.tosijs.net/skin-tone/index.md): A skin's colour from one dial, very fair (0) through to very dark (1), plus a redness dial for undertone.
- [skin-shading](https://3d.tosijs.net/skin-shading/index.md): Skin that reads as skin without a subsurface pipeline: three cheap terms a material plugin adds to a PBR material, lit by the scene's sun.
- [human-face](https://3d.tosijs.net/human-face/index.md): Eyes and eyelashes for a character builder body, and a gaze that looks at something.
- [human-expression](https://3d.tosijs.net/human-expression/index.md): A character builder face that blinks, talks and smiles. MakeHuman's CC0 face pose units (lids, jaw, lips, mouth corners, brows, cheeks, tongue: 59 of…

- [hair-shading](https://3d.tosijs.net/hair-shading/index.md): Hair coloured the way a colourist describes it: a BASE colour and a HIGHLIGHT colour. A material plugin tints the hair texture with the base, leans its…

- [body-sweep](https://3d.tosijs.net/body-sweep/index.md): Clothes, shoes and hair as SWEEPS: a profile taken from the body and carried along a path, with curves along the way.

- [Land and Sky](https://3d.tosijs.net/land-and-sky/index.md): THE KITCHEN SINK — one world that grows with the world-sim layer. Terrain (with live dials), a sea, weather over both, and the encoded sky behind.
- [City Drive](https://3d.tosijs.net/city-drive/index.md): A city in a landscape. A seeded city of Kenney's kits stands on ground flattened for it, with traffic, street lights, and lit windows at night.
- [Cross Country](https://3d.tosijs.net/cross-country/index.md): A small tank in open country: rolling hills, woods, lakes and the whole sky. Its tracks are forty links a side, carried round by the model's own animation…

## Core

- [Core](https://3d.tosijs.net/core/index.md): The scene itself, and the ways to put things in it. b3d is the one element everything else lives inside.
- [b3d](https://3d.tosijs.net/tosi-b3d/index.md): The root 3D scene container. All other components (b3dSun, b3dSkybox, b3dLoader, etc.) must be children of a b3d element.
- [demo-utils](https://3d.tosijs.net/demo-utils/index.md): Scene-setup helpers for examples and prototypes — the "when in doubt" defaults that make a scene look like a scene instead of a test harness.
- [b3d-loader](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-loader/index.md): Loads a GLB/glTF scene file into the 3D scene. Meshes named with -ignore are discarded. Imported point/spot lights have their intensity scaled by…
- [asset-url](https://3d.tosijs.net/asset-url/index.md): A tiny indirection for referencing hosted blobs (models, textures, audio, …) by a LOGICAL path, so demos/consumers aren't littered with a hostname and can…
- [Primitives: box, sphere, ground](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-primitives/index.md): A box, a sphere and a ground plane, as elements. The quickest way to put something in a scene: no model file, a material already on it, and it casts and…
- [make-mesh](https://3d.tosijs.net/make-mesh/index.md): El.make.box({ y: 1, color: '#c33', glow: 0.3 }) — Babylon primitives with the four things everyone forgets already done.
- [b3d-library](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-library/index.md): Asset library component. Loads a GLB file via LoadAssetContainer and holds it as a reusable parts catalog — nothing is added to the scene until you call…
- [glb-manifest](https://3d.tosijs.net/glb-manifest/index.md): Reading the catalogue a curated library carries inside itself. A GLB's JSON chunk holds attribution (asset.extras) and, for libraries built by…
- [agents](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-agent/index.md): A scene an agent can use. Each <tosi-b3d> offers tools under its own prefix, b3d_<scene>_…: its settings panel as named controls an agent reads, sets and…
- [agent driver](https://3d.tosijs.net/agent-driver/index.md): How an agent drives: with the controls, never by moving things. An AgentDriver turns a command into ControlInput each frame, which the controllable in…
- [scene description](https://3d.tosijs.net/scene-description/index.md): The 3D view in words, for a screen reader: what you are in, which way you face, the time of day, and the named things nearby with how far and which way.
- [b3d-prop](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-prop/index.md): A library model in the scene, and nothing else. A transform, a mesh name, and no behaviour, which is most of what populates a level.
- [Material Conventions](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-utils/index.md): These conventions apply to all meshes entering the scene — via b3d-loader, b3d-library, or any component that calls register().
- [Scene schemas](https://3d.tosijs.net/scene-schemas/index.md): JSON Schema for the scene primitives, so a consumer never hand-copies our attributes. No DOM, no Babylon — importable from a headless runner.

## Sky and light

- [Sky and light](https://3d.tosijs.net/sky-and-light/index.md): What lights the scene, and what is behind it. Most scenes want a sun (which is also where shadows come from) and fills the shadows; lamps are lights you…
- [b3d-skybox](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-skybox/index.md): Procedural sky with sun/moon cycle driven by time of day. Automatically controls a b3dSun sibling's direction, intensity, and color.
- [b3d-moon](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-moon/index.md): Extra moons, cosmetic. Put up to four inside a <tosi-b3d-skybox>. Each is a colour and a size at a place on the star sphere.
- [moon light](https://3d.tosijs.net/moon-light/index.md): Where a sky's night light comes from when it has moons of its own (<tosi-b3d-moon>): the brightest moon ABOVE the horizon, as bright as the part of it lit…
- [starfield-codec](https://3d.tosijs.net/starfield-codec/index.md): A starfield is DATA, not a picture — so store it as data. Six small RGBA faces where the channels are not colour but *position, brightness, colour index
- [light pollution](https://3d.tosijs.net/light-pollution/index.md): A lit town washes the stars out of its own sky. In the middle of a city at night only the brightest few show, under a warm glow along the horizon; drive…
- [Sun and shadows (b3d-shadows)](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-shadows/index.md): B3dSun — directional light + cascaded shadow generator. Add a <tosi-b3d-sun> inside <tosi-b3d> and every registered mesh starts casting shadows onto every
- [Ambient light (b3d-light)](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-light/index.md): Hemispheric ambient fill light. Wraps BABYLON.HemisphericLight. Cheap to render and never casts shadows — pair it with b3dSun for directional light that
- [Lamps](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-lamp/index.md): Lights you can see. b3dPointLight, b3dSpotLight and b3dAreaLight are placed lights that come with their own fixture geometry, cast shadows where Babylon…
- [Light program editor](https://3d.tosijs.net/curve-program/index.md): CurveProgram3d — the editor for a whole LightProgram: several curves that share one pair of split markers.
- [Light programs](https://3d.tosijs.net/light-modulation/index.md): A light's whole life as one curve. Pure, deterministic, Babylon-free: the model behind b3d-lamp's flicker, pulse, beacon and fade. To see one run on a
- [b3d-light-shafts](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-light-shafts/index.md): Light you can see: shafts of sun breaking through a broken sky, and rays fanning down from the surface when you are under the water.
- [b3d-fog](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-fog/index.md): Adds fog to a scene, useful for atmosphere and hiding distant tile pop-in. When syncSkybox is true, the fog color automatically tracks the sibling…
- [b3d-reflections](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-reflections/index.md): Auto-attaches a reflection probe to every mesh whose name contains _mirror (or -mirror). PBR materials get the cube texture as their reflection, and…
- [Ambient occlusion (SSAO)](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-ssao/index.md): Corners get darker. Where a wall meets the floor, where crates are stacked, under a ledge: real light does not reach in there, and a renderer without…
- [environment](https://3d.tosijs.net/environment/index.md): StudioEnvironment(scene) gives PBR materials something to reflect: a procedural studio, sky above, a bright horizon and a darker floor below, drawn on a…
- [shadow-decal](https://3d.tosijs.net/shadow-decal/index.md): A soft blob shadow — the oldest trick in real-time 3D, and still the right one in a lot of places.

## Weather and clouds

- [Weather and clouds](https://3d.tosijs.net/weather-and-clouds/index.md): Cloud, wind, storms and the things that drift in the air. One idea runs through all of it: weather is something every component asks about where it is, so…
- [b3d-cloud-deck](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-cloud-deck/index.md): A cloud LAYER, as a layer. One lit surface overhead with dark undersides and bright fringes, driven by a field you can dial from clear to overcast and…
- [cloud-shadows](https://3d.tosijs.net/cloud-shadows/index.md): Projected cloud shadows — the classic technique, and the only one that works over real terrain.
- [b3d-clouds](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-clouds/index.md): A cloud layer you can fly into — and lose the world inside.
- [b3d-weather-cell](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-weather-cell/index.md): A place whose weather differs — a lee behind a ridge, a squall, a storm — declared as a circle on the map with what it adds at its centre.
- [weather](https://3d.tosijs.net/weather/index.md): The one question every weather consumer asks: what is the weather here, now? weatherAt(base, cells, x, z) answers it from the scene's base weather plus…
- [wind](https://3d.tosijs.net/wind/index.md): One wind for the scene, and provinces that bend it. Pure — no DOM, no Babylon — so the composition rule can be tested without a sky.
- [b3d-lightning](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-lightning/index.md): Lightning and thunder from the weather. Put one in a scene; it watches every <tosi-b3d-weather-cell> with storminess and strikes
- [b3d-ambient](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-ambient/index.md): The stuff in the air, or in the water. Bubbles and motes when you're under; rain, snow, dust or drifting seeds when you're not.

## Terrain

- [Terrain](https://3d.tosijs.net/terrain/index.md): Ground that goes on for as long as you keep walking. b3d-terrain streams a procedural landscape with one shader from seafloor to mountain; its climate…
- [b3d-terrain](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-terrain/index.md): Procedural terrain generator using 3D Perlin noise sampled on a cylinder surface. Longitude (u) wraps seamlessly; latitude (v) reflects at the midpoint…
- [biome-chart](https://3d.tosijs.net/biome-chart/index.md): The pure biome-classification model under the procedural terrain shader (TERRAIN-SHADER-DESIGN.md): position → (u, v) into a Whittaker-style chart —
- [biome-plugin](https://3d.tosijs.net/biome-plugin/index.md): The Babylon half of the procedural terrain shader (TERRAIN-SHADER-DESIGN.md)
- [slope-profile](https://3d.tosijs.net/slope-profile/index.md): Levels adjustments for terrain — the Photoshop-curves idea applied to the noise field before amplitude. A profile remaps normalized height (0..1 → 0..1)
- [landform](https://3d.tosijs.net/landform/index.md): Authored landforms as terrain overrides — where slope-profiles remap the noise (levels curves), a landform forces a shape through it: a volcano
- [landform schemas](https://3d.tosijs.net/landform-schemas/index.md): The options of each authored landform (volcano, impactCrater, pad, gulley, cover) as JSON Schema, for a host that builds its editors from schemas or keeps…
- [Province climate](https://3d.tosijs.net/province-climate/index.md): What a province does to the weather — water, temperature and volcanism, each a curve over normalised distance from the province's centre. Pure: no DOM, no
- [terrainEditor3d](https://3d.tosijs.net/terrain-editor/index.md): An editor for a terrain, built FROM its schema. Every range, log track, unit and enum comes from sceneSchemas.terrain(), so the control cannot disagree…
- [gradient-filter](https://3d.tosijs.net/gradient-filter/index.md): A curve you can put a value through. PiecewiseLinearFilter maps 0..1 to 0..1 through a list of control points, with straight lines between them.
- [b3d-decorator](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-decorator/index.md): Rocks and trees on the terrain, by budget and by climate. Drop it into a scene with a <tosi-b3d-terrain>.
- [scatter](https://3d.tosijs.net/scatter/index.md): Where things grow: rocks and trees placed on terrain by budget and by climate. The function is scatterPlacements (a bare scatter would leak a common noun…
- [procedural-rock](https://3d.tosijs.net/procedural-rock/index.md): Rocks made from a seed, with no model file. rockGeometry returns the positions, normals and indices of one rock.
- [Carved landforms](https://3d.tosijs.net/sdf-lattice/index.md): Ground you can cut holes in. Caves, lava tubes, arches, sea caves, overhangs, mine shafts — everything a heightfield cannot say, because a heightfield has…
- [carve](https://3d.tosijs.net/carve/index.md): The shapes you cut caves out of, and the noise that stops them looking cut. Pure, deterministic, Babylon-free; the vocabulary patch-field composes and
- [patch-field](https://3d.tosijs.net/patch-field/index.md): Landform's volumetric sibling. Where a landform post-filters the terrain's HEIGHT, a patch post-filters its DENSITY — one dimension up, so it can
- [city-layout](https://3d.tosijs.net/city-layout/index.md): A city's plan from a grid and a seed: where the roads run, the blocks between them, and the lots in each block that a building stands on.
- [b3d-city](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-city/index.md): A city to drive around, built from a seed: roads, blocks of buildings, street lights, parked cars, traffic and lit windows. The plan is city-layout; this
- [city-traffic](https://3d.tosijs.net/city-traffic/index.md): Cars that drive round a city by themselves, on a plan from city-layout. Pure and seeded: no Babylon, no clock (time is the dt you step it by), so the same…
- [window-lights](https://3d.tosijs.net/window-lights/index.md): Lit windows at night. A material plugin that finds a building's window glass by its colour and lights some of the rooms behind it: warm lamplight mostly…

- [Water](https://3d.tosijs.net/water/index.md): A sea that knows its shore. b3d-water is the surface: waves, reflections, and with shore="on" the surf, shallows and sea ice that come from knowing where…
- [b3d-water](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-water/index.md): Water plane with reflections, waves, and underwater fog effect.
- [medium](https://3d.tosijs.net/medium/index.md): What is this stuff, where does it end, and how far in am I? A pure, Babylon-free description of the substance a thing is moving through — air, water…

## Effects

- [Effects](https://3d.tosijs.net/effects/index.md): Things that happen and are gone. Effects (volcanoes, geysers, splashes, explosions, fireballs, sparks: particles, light and sound on one clock, edited in…
- [b3d-effect](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-effect/index.md): Volcanoes, geysers, splashes, explosions, fireballs and sparks: particles, light and sound on one clock.
- [b3d-particles](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-particles/index.md): Declarative particle effect component wrapping Babylon.js ParticleSystem. Use it for fire, smoke, explosions, thrusters, weapon trails, and more.
- [b3d-sound](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-sound/index.md): Declarative audio component wrapping Babylon.js Sound. Supports both 2D (ambient/music) and 3D (positional/spatial) audio.
- [b3d-trail](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-trail/index.md): A ribbon left behind by anything that moves: contrails, missile smoke, the wake of a fast enemy.
- [b3d-exploder](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-exploder/index.md): Shatters a mesh into fragments and animates them flying apart. Works by extracting vertex data, partitioning triangles into spatial clusters…

- [aim IK](https://3d.tosijs.net/aim-ik/index.md): Point what is held where the aim goes, by turning the spine after the clips have posed the body.

- [character core](https://3d.tosijs.net/character-core/index.md): The character creator's working parts, for any engine. Twenty-nine modules make a character without Babylon or a DOM: they read MakeHuman's body, shape

- [b3d-interactive](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-interactive/index.md): Makes a mesh touchable. Point at it, reach it, use it — and it tells you, by callback or by bubbling event. It is the substrate doors, knobs, switches

- [b3d-trigger](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-trigger/index.md): Invisible proximity zone that fires callbacks and dispatches events when a target (the active camera or a named mesh) enters or exits a spherical region.
- [b3d-collisions](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-collisions/index.md): Opt-in collision detection via mesh naming conventions authored in Blender.
- [b3d-physics](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-physics/index.md): Enables Jolt physics on the scene. Add as a child of <tosi-b3d> to opt in to rigid-body simulation.
- [b3d-beacon](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-beacon/index.md): A clickable hull for anything that has a position and no geometry. A lamp is a light; a positional sound is a sound; a spawn point is a coordinate.
- [b3d-manipulator](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-manipulator/index.md): Translate, rotate and scale handles you can grab — with a mouse, a finger, or a hand in a headset. Drop it in a scene, point it at an element or a mesh

## World Sim

- [World Sim](https://3d.tosijs.net/world-sim/index.md): A world that something else can drive. The simulation holds the state and resolves what physically happens; an outside driver (a story engine, a script
- [world-contract](https://3d.tosijs.net/world-contract/index.md): The boundary between the simulation (tosijs-3d) and an external driver (an AI narrative engine, a scripted demo, anything).
- [world-store](https://3d.tosijs.net/world-store/index.md): A pure, Babylon-free, deterministic reference implementation of world-contract.
- [world-view](https://3d.tosijs.net/world-view/index.md): The Babylon view of a world-store. The store is the authoritative, serializable truth; the view is a disposable projection of it.
- [inventory](https://3d.tosijs.net/inventory/index.md): One inventory model for a party, a loadout and a starship designer. Pure and Babylon-free: things, the holders they are in, and moves between them that…
- [inventory-box](https://3d.tosijs.net/inventory-box/index.md): An inventory holder on a panel, wired to carry's drag and drop: its slots are sockets, its lists are tiles with a place to drop, and every drop is checked…
- [min-sim-conformance](https://3d.tosijs.net/min-sim-conformance/index.md): One contract, two stores. The coordinate-free MinSimApi (world-contract §8) is implemented by BOTH Ariosto's reference store and tosijs-3d's world-store.
- [b3d-spawner](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-spawner/index.md): Keeps the world populated. Spawns prefabs — usually encounters: a mothership with escorts, a base with ground defences and air cover — around the player…
- [formations](https://3d.tosijs.net/formations/index.md): Pure, deterministic placement patterns — where the members of an encounter stand relative to its centre.
- [prefab](https://3d.tosijs.net/prefab/index.md): A prefab is a named factory that instantiates a package of stuff at a pose — the concept Unity calls a prefab, and one this library needed a name for.
- [b3d-death](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-death/index.md): Death needs an exit. Without one, a crash is a dead end: the input manager stays welded to the wreck, you go on "flying" a corpse, and the game is stuck.

## Space

- [Space](https://3d.tosijs.net/space/index.md): Stars, planets and the galaxy they are in, generated from a seed. A for any star in it, planets with atmospheres, and a black hole.
- [b3d-galaxy](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-galaxy/index.md): Procedural galaxy renderer — the voxel galaxy, the one galaxy implementation, drawn: thousands of stars in a spiral arm distribution, each
- [voxel-galaxy](https://3d.tosijs.net/voxel-galaxy/index.md): A galaxy as a grid of voxels, each with two derived seeds — one for its BRIGHT stars, one for its DIM stars.
- [b3d-star-system](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-star-system/index.md): Renders an individual star system with a procedural star and its planets. Given a galaxy seed and a star's ADDRESS (star, stable) or index (starIndex) in…
- [b3d-star](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-star/index.md): Procedural star: a sphere with a shader surface. What makes it read as a ball rather than a white disc is limb darkening: toward the edge you look through…
- [b3d-planet](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-planet/index.md): Procedural planet mesh using a subdivided cube projected onto a sphere. Height displacement from 3D Perlin noise (gross + detail layers) with gradient…
- [gas-giant](https://3d.tosijs.net/gas-giant/index.md): The cloud tops of a gas giant, as one shader function. Banded, sheared by winds that alternate direction from belt to belt, with a long-lived storm.
- [rocky-world](https://3d.tosijs.net/rocky-world/index.md): What kind of rock a planet is, as data: the Moon, Mercury, Mars, Venus, Io, Titan, an ice moon and an Earth, each a sea, an air, clouds, relief, craters…
- [b3d-black-hole](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-black-hole/index.md): Procedural black hole with accretion disk, gravitational lensing effect, and photon ring. Inspired by the Interstellar visualization — not physically…
- [sphere-map](https://3d.tosijs.net/sphere-map/index.md): Where a place on the ground is on the globe, and back. A terrain in surfaceType="sphere" is a flat sheet wrapped round a planet: walk far enough east and…
- [planet-map](https://3d.tosijs.net/planet-map/index.md): A real world from its maps. NASA and NOAA publish the height of the Moon, Mars and the Earth as flat images, one pixel per patch of latitude and…
- [space-backdrop](https://3d.tosijs.net/space-backdrop/index.md): Space, set up once: a sun and the encoded star sky with no air, the galaxy's band tipped off the scene's horizontal plane.

## Performance

- [Performance](https://3d.tosijs.net/performance/index.md): One scene, a phone and a workstation. The probe measures the device once and sorts it into a tier; components then resolve any setting left
- [b3d-probe](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-probe/index.md): <tosi-b3d-probe> — a device-capability probe. Drop it anywhere (a landing page is ideal): it benchmarks the device once, and every <tosi-b3d> on the…
- [perf-probe](https://3d.tosijs.net/perf-probe/index.md): Pure, Babylon-free core for the device-capability probe (see b3d-probe for the component that actually runs the benchmark).
- [b3d-quality](https://3d.tosijs.net/b3d-quality/index.md): The system quality proxy — the single place that vends device-appropriate defaults. The probe measures the device and feeds a PerfProfile in here…
- [Cost sweep](https://3d.tosijs.net/cost-sweep/index.md): Where a frame goes, measured on the device it runs on. The sweep switches one thing off at a time (a group of meshes, the render targets, the shadows)
- [Draw order](https://3d.tosijs.net/draw-order/index.md): Babylon draws opaque meshes in the order they were created. Nothing looks wrong that way, because the depth buffer sorts out who is in front, but every…
- [debug-sink](https://3d.tosijs.net/debug-sink/index.md): Somewhere for a page to send what it would otherwise print: a headset has no console, so its readings have to go somewhere you can read them afterwards.

## utilities

- [utilities](https://3d.tosijs.net/utilities/index.md): - clock - undo history
- [clock](https://3d.tosijs.net/clock/index.md): Game code does not read the wall clock. Time in a simulation comes from the simulation: sceneDelta(scene) for a frame's step and sceneSeconds(scene)
- [undo history](https://3d.tosijs.net/undo-history/index.md): A list of states and a place in it: the one undo model behind the character builder and the rig tool. A tool records its whole state after each change that

## Reference

- [Reference](https://3d.tosijs.net/reference/index.md): The seeded random sources and noise everything procedural is built on.
- [Pseudo Random Numbers](https://3d.tosijs.net/mersenne-twister/index.md): Randomness you can replay. Everything procedural here (a galaxy, a planet's craters, where the rocks go, who spawns) is drawn from a generator started…
- [perlin-noise](https://3d.tosijs.net/perlin-noise/index.md): Seeded 3D Perlin noise. The same seed always gives the same field, which is what terrain, clouds and everything else procedural here is built on.
- [Noise texture](https://3d.tosijs.net/noise-texture/index.md): Shader noise read instead of computed. Arithmetic noise in a fragment shader is the expensive way to get noise: eight hashed corners a sample, every…

## Docs

- [Design notes](https://3d.tosijs.net/design-notes/index.md): Remarks of Tonio Loewald's that decided how something works. The reference pages say what is true now and why; this page keeps the original words, with a…
- [Acknowledgements](https://3d.tosijs.net/acknowledgements/index.md): Tosijs-3d stands on other people's work: models, maps, measurements, icons, libraries and ideas.
